entities.summary:
The computer monitor is a crucial component of modern computing, revolutionizing the way people interact with digital information.

Born in the mid-20th century, computer monitors were initially bulky and expensive, but their design and functionality improved significantly over the years.

By the 1980s, computer monitors had become a ubiquitous part of offices, homes, and public spaces, with the introduction of the first flat-screen monitors in the 1990s.

Today, computer monitors come in a range of sizes, resolutions, and technologies, from LED and LCD to OLED and plasma.

The impact of computer monitors on society has been profound, enabling people to access vast amounts of information, communicate with others across the globe, and engage in creative pursuits.

As technology continues to evolve, computer monitors will likely play an increasingly important role in shaping the future of human interaction and innovation.
